title: Four Seasons In: How CourtIQ's Model Has Gotten Sharper Every Year
author: Doc
summary: Four full seasons of graded picks are in the book. Doc walks through the accuracy trend season by season — and previews the data behind night one of 2026-27.

content.value:
## The Number That Matters

Four full seasons of graded picks are now in the record book. The question worth asking isn't whether the model called more games right than wrong — at this sample size, 68.8% last season, that's not in doubt. It's whether the model is actually *improving*, or just running hot.

### Why It's Climbing, Not Just Varying

Four points in a row, every one higher than the last, isn't what noise usually looks like. The likelier explanation is the less exciting one: more seasons of net-rating and pace data to carry forward, better-calibrated absence handling, and four years of graded games to check the calibration curve against instead of one.

That doesn't mean next season lands above 70% — it means the model has earned a little more benefit of the doubt than it had a year ago.

### Night One, By the Numbers

2026-27 doesn't have a graded game yet, but the opening slate is already on the board.

editor_note: These opening-night numbers are current team ratings carried over from last season — they'll move once rosters are set and the first injury reports of 2026-27 land.
